## The question

Every month USDA's **World Agricultural Supply and Demand Estimates**
(WASDE) project the U.S. corn yield and the price farmers will receive.
The first projection for a crop comes in May and is revised every month
until January. In May 2012 USDA projected 166.0 bushels per acre; the
drought brought it to 123.4. How did the May forecasts of yield and price
hold up from 2000 to 2026, and what did the world price do meanwhile?

## Target

![Target figure](https://arielortizbobea.github.io/assets/data/hw3_target.png)

## Data

1. **The list of WASDE reports: an API.** USDA's ESMIS archive returns
   every report since 1973 as JSON, 25 per page, with the URLs of each
   report's files:
   <https://esmis.nal.usda.gov/api/v1/release/findByIdentifier/wasde?latest=false&page=0>
2. **The reports themselves: downloads, read with regular expressions.**
   Take the `.txt` file of each report, or the `.xml` when there is no
   text. The yield and the price are in the CORN block of the table "U.S.
   Feed Grain and Corn Supply and Use".
3. **The world price of corn: a CSV.** FRED series `PMAIZMTUSDM`, dollars
   per metric ton (one ton is 39.368 bushels):
   <https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=PMAIZMTUSDM>

USDA's `robots.txt` asks for ten seconds between requests. Save every file
you download and never download it twice. Save each report under
`data/wasde/` plus the part of its URL after `release-files/`, so
`…/release-files/3t945q76s/ms35t8930/t435gd264/wasde-08-10-2012.xml` goes
to `data/wasde/3t945q76s/ms35t8930/t435gd264/wasde-08-10-2012.xml`.

## Output

- `figures/hw3_target.png`, 12 × 8.4 inches at 220 dpi.
- `data_clean/corn_forecasts.csv`: one row per report, with its date,
  season, yield and price.
- `data_clean/corn_world_price.csv`: one row per month.
- `NOTES.md`: how you chose the files, your patterns, your checks and
  what each would catch, and an AI disclosure (tools, uses, what you
  checked).

## Figure rules

- One line per season, from the May report to the January report, each
  point at its report's release date.
- Top panel: the yield. Bottom panel: the price projection (the midpoint
  when USDA gives a range), over the monthly world price in grey.
- Colour: warm when the January yield ended below May, cool when above,
  darker as the gap grows. The price line takes its season's colour. The
  season still open is yellow.
- An open circle at May, a white dot at January, on a dark background.

Font, exact shades and the key's layout are never differences.

## How to submit

Your repository is **`hw3-<your github username>`** in the course
organization. It holds only a README that links to this page; the
project's layout is yours to set up. Put the code in `code/`, with `code/run_everything.R`
running it all, and paths relative to the project root. Commit as you go;
the grader runs the last commit pushed before the deadline from a fresh
clone.
